ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram shows a 24 V power supply on the left, with the upper end of the power supply connected to a series resistor labeled 1.2 kΩ; after the series resistor it reaches the output node. This output node is connected downward in parallel to a Zener diode labeled Vz = 7.9 V to ground, and at the same time the right side of the output node is also connected in parallel to the load resistor Rload to ground. Reasoning calculation: The problem gives Rload = 910 Ω. Under the assumption that the Zener diode is operating in voltage regulation, the output node voltage is 7.9 V. The series resistor current is Iseries = (24 - 7.9) / 1200 = 16.1 / 1200 A = 0.0134167 A = 13.4167 mA. The load current is Iload = 7.9 / 910 A = 0.0086813 A = 8.6813 mA. From KCL at the output node, Izener = Iseries - Iload = 13.4167 - 8.6813 = 4.7354 mA, approximately 4.74 mA.

Assume the zener is regulating, so the output/load voltage is 7.9 V. Compute the current through the 1.2 kΩ resistor as (24 - 7.9)/1200 A. Compute the load current as 7.9/910 A. Use KCL at the output node and subtract the load current from the series current to obtain the zener current in mA.

method.method_draft: Describe the image as a one-port supply made of 24 V and 1.2 kΩ feeding a shunt zener/load node. Convert that supply side to a Norton equivalent: IN = 24/1200 A with parallel resistance 1.2 kΩ. From the text, use Rload = 910 Ω. Since the zener clamps the node to 7.9 V, compute the current through the Norton parallel resistance as 7.9/1200 A and through the load as 7.9/910 A. Subtract both from the Norton source current to get the zener current, then convert to mA.
